clue.text: Vented one's feelings, having fired the second eleven

parts.note: to fire a gun is to let it off
a cricket or football eleven is a team

explanation.surface: A club sacks its reserve side and someone lets rip about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second eleven' reads as a reserve side, but it splits into S (second) and TEAM (eleven).
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing pent-up emotion is the idiom of venting, borrowed from boilers releasing pressure.

clue.text: Be up for immorality?

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to be is to exist, or live

explanation.surface: A question of whether someone is all in favour of wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be up for' reads as 'be keen on', but 'up' turns LIVE (be) around.
explanation.definitionFit: Wickedness or sinfulness is the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Has some topless evening wear

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: gowns are formal evening dresses

explanation.surface: Someone has a saucy line of topless evening dresses.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it.

clue.text: Hot property dealing in rails

explanation.surface: Trading stolen goods through a fence.
explanation.definitionFit: Receiving stolen goods is the slang sense of fencing; a run of railings round a field is also fencing.

clue.text: Look up to the very best

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to look at or notice something is to spot it

explanation.surface: Advice to admire the finest people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look up to' reads as 'admire'; in fact 'up' turns SPOT (look) around.
explanation.definitionFit: Something supreme or excellent is informally said to be the tops.

clue.text: Weapons lifted from aeroplane's racks

indicators.note: lifted says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Arms taken from the racks of a military plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' in a down clue reads the hidden letters LANESRA upwards; 'from' signals that they are taken out of the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A store or collection of arms is an arsenal.

clue.text: Pre-school beats tabloid on boxing match

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a tabloid is a popular newspaper, a paper
a boxing match is fought in rounds

explanation.surface: Children's fighting is covered by a gossip rag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beats' reads as blows; it means regular routes, the newspaper deliveries a child does before school.
explanation.definitionFit: Delivery routes walked early in the morning by children are fittingly called beats.

clue.text: Find a new way of saying "poachers in a muddle"

definitions.text: Find a new way of saying

indicators.note: a muddle is a jumble, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Rephrase the words 'poachers in a muddle'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a' looks like part of the indicator, but both words are fodder: POACHERS IN A has exactly the eleven letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To invent a new expression is the idiom for creating a fresh way of saying something.

clue.text: Mexican food firm chasing volunteers

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the firm comes after the volunteers

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A food company pursues people who offered to help.
explanation.definitionFit: A folded tortilla with filling is a classic dish from Mexico.

clue.text: On course at last for an attractive job?

explanation.surface: Someone finally on track for a glamorous position.
explanation.definitionFit: The finishing line on a racecourse is where a race ends; whimsically, a job that wins you over is a desirable post.

clue.text: Ecstasy hidden in French wine vessel

indicators.note: hidden in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: vin is the French word for wine
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A drug smuggled inside a container of French wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood vessel carrying blood to the heart is a vein.

clue.text: Goes along with current organisations

parts.note: AC is alternating current
companies are business organisations

explanation.surface: Someone follows whatever groups are fashionable now.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort or travel with someone is to keep them company.

clue.text: Good people support Asian country's interminable outrage

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means sitting underneath the other piece
interminable means without end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: India is a country in Asia
a people is a nation

explanation.surface: Decent people back a great nation's endless anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' cuts INDIA to INDI; 'support' puts G NATION below it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Anger at unfairness is a strong synonym for outrage.

clue.text: Quietly satisfied with the subject matter

explanation.surface: A calm pleasure taken in the topic under discussion.
explanation.definitionFit: Being pleased in a quiet way is one sense; the material contained in a book or talk is the other.

clue.text: Rib gets tight around mid-evening

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: taut means pulled tight

indicators.note: mid means the middle letter of the word evening

explanation.surface: A dig that tightens up around the middle of a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: To rib someone is to tease or jeer at them.

clue.text: An excursion that provides pay dirt, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps suggests these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: An outing that pays off like striking gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pay dirt' is ore worth mining, but here it is just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-day outing is a short excursion.

clue.text: Financial obligation about university entrance

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a debt is money owed

explanation.surface: Student loans arrive as one enters university.
explanation.definitionFit: A first appearance, such as a performer's, is a debut.

clue.text: Presented apprentice with hammer

parts.note: presented means gave
L stands for learner, an apprentice, from L-plates

explanation.surface: A trainee is handed a hammer as a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: A gavel is a small mallet used by a judge or auctioneer.

clue.text: God's love facing commotion

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a din is a loud noise or commotion

explanation.surface: A deity's affection set against a noisy uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief deity of Norse mythology.

clue.text: Show pleasure when voting system covers ancient city

indicators.note: covers means the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: PR is proportional representation
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Satisfaction when a voting system embraces an old city.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat makes this low sound to display contentment.

clue.text: Hot and cold, you are said to suffer

parts.note: hot and in both mean fashionable
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: said means the words are spoken and heard as letters

parts.note: the words you are, spoken, sound like the letters U and R

explanation.surface: Blowing hot and cold, a person reportedly endures it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring something unwelcome on oneself, like a loss or penalty, is to suffer it.

clue.text: Sort of person to feel at home with Castro?

indicators.note: with joins the two pieces side by side

parts.note: in means at home
Fidel Castro was the Cuban revolutionary leader

explanation.surface: Who would feel comfortable alongside the Cuban leader?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to feel' joins the parts: one who feels at home with Fidel, playfully an unbeliever.
explanation.definitionFit: A non-believer in a particular religion is a type of person.

clue.text: Reply given by priest worried about love

indicators.note: about means one piece goes round the other
worried means the letters are shaken up and rearranged

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An anxious clergyman answers a question about romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges PRIEST to RIPST, which goes 'about' O.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick, sharp retort is a riposte.

clue.text: Sharp chap follows a play on words

indicators.note: follows means the chap comes after the pun

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
a gent is a man or chap

explanation.surface: A witty fellow comes after some wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting or acrid, as of a smell or remark.

clue.text: Outbursts whenever it's read out

indicators.note: out means the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Rants erupt whenever something is read aloud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read out' looks like a phrase, but 'out' rearranges ITSREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Long angry speeches are a kind of verbal outburst.

clue.text: Written record of books found in Newcastle

indicators.note: found in means one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: NE is the postcode area for Newcastle upon Tyne
OT is the Old Testament, the books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A record of a library's stock in a northern city.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written jotting or memo.

clue.text: Hide from rain

explanation.surface: Shelter from a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal's skin is a pelt; to rain hard is to pelt down.

clue.text: Not really dropping the odds for this exam

indicators.note: dropping the odd letters keeps the second, fourth, sixth and eighth

explanation.surface: Advice that this test isn't really about chance.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoken test, such as a language viva, is an oral.

clue.text: Intend appearance to be reported

indicators.note: to be reported says the word is spoken and heard rather than written

parts.note: mien is a person's look or appearance

explanation.surface: Someone plans to have their looks written up.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something in mind as a purpose.

clue.text: Mostly negative sign from opponents

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: adverse means unfavourable or negative
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Largely gloomy omens come from rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Enemies or rivals are adversaries.

clue.text: Love affair so ends at last, finding god

indicators.note: at last means take the final letter of each word

explanation.surface: A romance ends, so finally a deity appears.
explanation.walkthrough: The final letters of 'Love affair so ends' spell it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek deity of love.

clue.text: Washing up — and drying!

parts.note: not dishes: the laundry hung up on a cord outside to dry

explanation.definitionFit: A cord where laundry hangs to dry outdoors.
